name: Valleyball Versus
summary:
Valleyball Versus is a physics-based sports game in which two sides try to knock a ball through the opposing side’s raised hoop inside an enclosed, valley-shaped arena. The athletes are physically simulated ragdolls with oversized, club-like hands, so every strike, slide, dive, fall and collision comes out of the physics simulation rather than canned animation. Play is continuous: there are no fouls, no out-of-bounds and no restarts. Instead, each goal swaps the ends the two sides are attacking while the ball stays in play.

Matches are played one-on-one or two-on-two on a shared screen or in split screen, against or alongside computer-controlled athletes at three difficulty levels. The ball comes in three sizes that double as the difficulty setting, from a large ball that is the easiest to play to a small one that demands precise strikes. A practice mode puts all three balls on the court at once.
